schemes.english_name: Graduate Policy Workshops, Master in Public Affairs
schemes.description: Required second-year MPA workshop: each workshop has 8-10 students working in a team on a policy problem for a real-world client (government agency, multilateral organisation or nonprofit), with field research during fall break, a final report and a presentation to the client.
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Master in Public Affairs (MPA) students after first year
schemes.project_evidence: Each workshop produces a final report and presentation to the client [2].
schemes.group_evidence: 'Each workshop consists of eight to 10 students who work in teams to evaluate a policy challenge' [2]; 'working in teams ... producing client-ready reports' [1].
schemes.employer_evidence: Workshops respond to 'the needs of real-world clients - such as government agencies, multilateral organisations, or nonprofits - whose challenges serve as the basis for the courses'; students present to the client [1][2]. Wording 'usually for real-world clients' [2] means coverage is the norm but not guaranteed per workshop.
schemes.partner_role: Client: sets policy challenge; receives report and presentation; hosts field visit
schemes.deliverable: Client-ready policy report + presentation to client

profile_md: Princeton has one strongly verified route and several partial ones, spread across units rather than institution-wide. **SPIA Graduate Policy Workshops (SPI 591)** are required in the MPA: teams of 8-10 work on briefs for real clients (government agencies, multilateral organisations, nonprofits), do field research and present a report to the client (Fall 2025 confirmed). The undergraduate **Policy Task Force (SPI 301)** is a compulsory junior group project for SPIA concentrators but no external client is evidenced; the **Policy Advocacy Clinic** works with named external policy partners (ACLU, lawmakers) but team structure is unstated. The Keller Center's **Community Project Studios / Tiger Challenge** places student teams with nonprofit and government partners (Summer 2026 partner Smith Family Foundation), open across majors, but current delivery is unconfirmed. **ProCES** is an umbrella supporting community-engaged courses; qualifying examples include COS 333 (some teams build for nonprofits) and a 2025 workers-technology seminar (historical). No business, law or medical school exists; most engineering capstones lack documented external sponsors. ProCES and some CS pages blocked page access (Cloudflare/403), so those items rest on search extracts.
gaps: proces.princeton.edu and gradfutures.princeton.edu returned Cloudflare challenges and were not accessed (not bypassed); cs.princeton.edu course pages 403. Per-course ProCES evidence, Keller Design minor project course, EGR 200, architecture studios, GradFUTURES capstones, department-level engineering capstones (further instances likely) not researched.
